mainTopic: Laws of insulating food for שבת (הטמנה): moist materials, permitted materials, the story of אלישע בעל כנפים, and moving hides and fleece.
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier topic. רבנן made two strict rules about when a tool's parts count as connected, one for טומאה and one for הזאה. The גמרא then asks whether the משנה's ban on insulating in 'moist' materials means only naturally moist materials, or also materials that got wet. Two proofs are tried, and both are pushed off with wool plucked from between an animal's thighs, which is naturally damp, so the question stays unresolved. A new משנה lists materials that may be used for הטמנה, including doves' wings. That mention leads to the story of אלישע בעל כנפים, whose תפילין miraculously turned into doves' wings, because ישראל is like a dove protected by its wings, the מצוות. A ברייתא then proves that רבי יהודה's fine-versus-coarse ruling is about flax chaff. Another משנה teaches that hides may be moved on שבת but wool fleece may not, and it records a dispute about taking a pot out of a basket of fleece. The גמרא asks whether a craftsman's hides may also be moved. רבי יונתן בן אלעזר answers from logic, and רבי חנינא בר חמא begins quoting רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, whose words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: רבנן's two stricter decrees about connection
steps.stepSummary: רבנן made two stricter rules. For טומאה, a tool's parts count as connected even when the tool is not being used. For הזאה, the parts do not count as connected even when the tool is being used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן decreed about impurity: even when the tool is not in use, it counts as connected, because when it is in use it is connected. And they decreed about sprinkling: even when the tool is in use, it does not count as connected, because when it is not in use it is not connected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion about tools made of parts, like scissors. It adds two stricter rules that רבנן made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the parts count as one unit (חיבור) only while the tool is being used. רבנן were strict in both directions. For טומאה, they treat the parts as connected all the time, so impurity spreads to every part. For הזאה, they treat the parts as separate all the time, so each part must be sprinkled on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis made a decree (a protective rule)
While the tool is being used for work
Sprinkling the purifying water (of the red heifer)

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases רבנן chose the strict side. For טומאה the parts are always connected, so impurity spreads. For הזאה the parts are never connected, so each part needs its own sprinkling.
steps.confusionAlert: The two decrees go in opposite directions, yet both are strict. They are not contradicting each other.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis decreed regarding impurity
when it is not at the time of use
because of impurity at the time of use;
phrases.notes: Not in use counts as connected, because in use it is connected.

phrases.english: and regarding sprinkling at the time of use
because of sprinkling when not at the time of use.
phrases.notes: In use does not count as connected, because when not in use it is not connected.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגָזְרוּ רַבָּנַן עַל טוּמְאָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the previous sugya, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbinically, a tool's parts are always connected for טומאה and never connected for הזאה.

steps.title: What kind of moistness does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'when they are moist.' It asks whether this means moist by nature or also moist from an outside source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'when they are moist.' A question was asked: Does this mean moist on their own, or perhaps moist because of something else?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic. It quotes a phrase from the משנה about insulating food and asks what that phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids insulating (הטמנה) a pot in certain materials when they are moist. The question is about how far the rule reaches. One option is that it covers only materials that are naturally moist. The other option is that it also covers dry materials that got wet.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked by them (the scholars)
Because of something else (an outside source)

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides whether wet material that is normally dry is forbidden for הטמנה.

phrases.english: "When they are moist."
They asked:
Moist on their own (naturally),

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא לַחִין מֵחֲמַת דָּבָר אַחֵר.
phrases.english: or perhaps moist because of something else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does לחין mean naturally moist, or also moistened from outside?

steps.title: Proof from soft wool in the משנה's list
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists מוכין (soft wool) among the moist materials. Wool is not naturally moist, so the rule must include materials that are moist from an outside source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Not in straw, not in grape residue, not in soft wool, and not in grass, when they are moist. It makes sense if you say moist from something else. But if you say moist on their own, how can you find soft wool that is moist on its own?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question using the משנה's own list of materials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw, grape residue, and grass can be naturally moist, but wool is normally dry. If the משנה meant only natural moistness, listing מוכין would make no sense. So the attempted proof is that 'moist' includes things made wet from outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (an attempted proof is coming)
Soft materials, such as wool scraps
Grape skins and residue left after pressing
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Not in straw and not in grape residue
and not in soft wool and not in grass
when they are moist.
It works well if you say
moist because of something else; that is fine.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לַחִין מֵחֲמַת עַצְמָן,
phrases.english: But if you say moist on their own,
soft wool that is moist on its own,
how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That לחין includes moisture from an outside source.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists מוכין, which are not naturally moist.

steps.title: Rejected: wool from between the thighs
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Wool plucked from between an animal's thighs is naturally damp from sweat.
steps.simpleTranslation: From wool plucked from between the thighs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by showing a case where wool really is naturally moist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that wool is never naturally moist. Wool from the thigh area is damp with the animal's sweat, so the משנה can still mean only natural moistness. The question stays open.

phrases.english: From wool plucked from between the thighs.
phrases.notes: That wool is damp from sweat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed that wool can never be naturally moist.

steps.title: Second proof from רבי אושעיא's moist garment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אושעיא forbids insulating in a moist garment. A garment is not naturally moist, so this seems to show that outside moisture counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what רבי אושעיא taught: One may insulate in a dry garment and in dry produce, but not in a moist garment or moist produce. How can you find a garment that is moist on its own?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that seems to support the same side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce can be naturally moist, but cloth seems to become moist only from outside. So רבי אושעיא's 'moist garment' looks like a case of outside moisture. This would challenge the view that only natural moistness counts.

keyTerms.meaning: And that which was taught (in a ברייתא)
An early אמורא who collected ברייתות
We insulate (cover the pot to keep it hot)

phrases.english: And that which Rabbi Oshaya taught:
We may insulate in a dry garment
and in dry produce,
but not in a moist garment
and not in moist produce.
A garment moist on its own,
how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempted proof, after the first one was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That outside moisture counts as לחין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אושעיא about a moist garment.

steps.title: Same rejection: cloth from thigh wool
steps.stepSummary: The same answer is given again. The garment was woven from damp thigh wool, so it is naturally moist.
steps.simpleTranslation: From wool plucked from between the thighs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same answer to reject the second proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment was spun and woven from thigh wool while that wool was still damp. So even a garment can be naturally moist. Neither proof works, and the גמרא leaves the question unresolved.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail because of one case: wool from between the thighs is naturally moist. It is still unknown whether outside moisture counts as לחין.

phrases.english: From wool plucked from between the thighs.
phrases.notes: The cloth was made from that damp wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 5 with the same answer as step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי אושעיא's ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed that a garment can never be naturally moist.

steps.title: New משנה: Materials Allowed for Insulating
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists materials that may be used for insulating a pot for שבת. רבי יהודה forbids fine flax chaff but permits coarse flax chaff.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may insulate in clothing and in produce, in doves' wings, in carpenters' wood-shavings, and in fine flax chaff. רבי יהודה forbids fine chaff and permits coarse chaff.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists materials that are permitted for wrapping a pot to keep it hot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה listed materials that are forbidden because they add heat. This משנה lists the opposite: materials that only keep the existing heat in. רבי יהודה holds that fine flax chaff does add heat, so he forbids it and allows only the coarse kind.

keyTerms.meaning: We may insulate (wrap a pot to keep it hot)
Chaff or waste fibers of flax

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets out the permitted side of the laws of הטמנה. The words 'doves' wings' also become the springboard for the אגדה that follows.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may insulate in clothing and in produce,
in doves' wings and in carpenters' wood-shavings,
phrases.notes: The phrase 'doves' wings' is what triggers the גמרא's discussion below.

phrases.english: and in fine flax chaff.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר בַּדַּקָּה וּמַתִּיר בַּגַּסָּה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda forbids the fine and permits the coarse.
phrases.notes: In his view, fine chaff adds heat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of moist materials ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clothing, produce, doves' wings, wood-shavings and fine flax chaff may be used for insulating. רבי יהודה permits only coarse flax chaff.

steps.title: תפילין Need a Clean Body Like אלישע
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי teaches that wearing תפילין requires a clean body, like that of אלישע בעל כנפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי ינאי said: תפילין require a clean body, like אלישע, 'Man of Wings.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that has nothing to do with insulating. It is linked to the משנה only by the words 'doves' wings.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה mentioned doves' wings, the גמרא quotes a teaching about אלישע, who was called 'Man of Wings.' The legal point is that a person wearing תפילין must keep his body clean. אלישע is the model of someone who guarded his תפילין carefully.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not אלישע הנביא, the prophet. It is a later חסיד from the time of Roman rule. Also, this section is not about insulating at all. It is connected to the משנה only by the words 'doves' wings.'

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yannai said:
Tefillin require a clean body,
like Elisha, 'Man of Wings.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: תְּפִילִּין צְרִיכִין גּוּף נָקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the words 'doves' wings' from the משנה and moves to a related teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wearing תפילין requires a clean body.

steps.title: What Does 'Clean Body' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי ינאי meant by a 'clean body.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase 'clean body.' This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'clean body' is vague. It could refer to physical cleanliness, or to some specific behavior while wearing תפילין. The גמרא wants a precise definition.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request for a definition)

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'clean body' mean for wearing תפילין?

steps.title: אביי and רבא Define a Clean Body
steps.stepSummary: אביי says it means not passing wind while wearing them. רבא says it means not sleeping while wearing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: that he should not pass wind in them. רבא said: that he should not sleep in them.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different explanations of 'clean body.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי understands 'clean' literally: one must not pass wind while wearing תפילין. רבא understands it as a matter of awareness: one must not fall asleep in them, since he may then pass wind without noticing or lose focus on the תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often debates רבא
An אמורא, אביי's frequent partner in debate

phrases.english: Abaye said: that he should not pass wind in them.
Rava said: that he should not sleep in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with two views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: no passing wind while wearing תפילין. רבא: no sleeping while wearing תפילין.

steps.title: Why Was אלישע Called Man of Wings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אלישע was given the name 'Man of Wings.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call him 'Man of Wings'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the origin of אלישע's nickname. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that 'clean body' has been explained, the גמרא turns to the other unclear part of רבי ינאי's statement, the title 'בעל כנפים.'

phrases.english: And why do they call him 'Man of Wings'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי ינאי's statement to explain the nickname.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind the title 'בעל כנפים.'

steps.title: The Story of the Roman Decree and the Miracle
steps.stepSummary: Rome decreed death for anyone wearing תפילין. אלישע wore them anyway. When an officer caught him, he said he was holding doves' wings, and his תפילין miraculously became doves' wings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, the wicked Roman kingdom decreed that anyone who wears תפילין would have his brain pierced. אלישע would wear them and go out to the marketplace. An officer saw him. אלישע ran from him, and the officer ran after him. When the officer reached him, אלישע took the תפילין off his head and held them in his hand. The officer said: What is this in your hand? אלישע said: Doves' wings. He opened his hand, and doves' wings were found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story about אלישע's self-sacrifice for תפילין and a miracle that saved him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע kept the מצוה of תפילין in public despite a death decree. When he was caught, he did not deny the מצוה with a lie. Instead, a miracle made his words true. This story explains both his nickname and why he is the model of guarding תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: They would pierce his brain (a death penalty)

phrases.english: Because once there decreed

phrases.aramaic: מַלְכוּת רוֹמִי הָרְשָׁעָה שְׁמָד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: the wicked kingdom of Rome a persecution against Israel,
that anyone who puts on tefillin,
they would pierce his brain.
And Elisha would put them on and go out to the marketplace.
An officer saw him;
he (Elisha) ran from him, and he (the officer) ran after him.
And when he reached him,
he (Elisha) took them off his head and held them in his hand.
He (the officer) said to him: What is this in your hand?
He said to him: Doves' wings.
He opened his hand,
and doves' wings were found.
phrases.notes: A miracle: the תפילין turned into doves' wings.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁפַּעַם אַחַת גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת רוֹמִי הָרְשָׁעָה שְׁמָד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלישע's תפילין miraculously became doves' wings when a Roman officer caught him.

steps.title: Therefore He Is Called אלישע, Man of Wings
steps.stepSummary: Because of this miracle, people called him 'אלישע בעל כנפים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore they call him 'אלישע, Man of Wings.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story by tying it back to the nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story fully answers the question of step 11. The name commemorates the miracle of the doves' wings.

phrases.english: Therefore they call him
'Elisha, Man of Wings.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the story of step 12 and answers step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The nickname 'בעל כנפים' commemorates the miracle of the doves' wings.

steps.title: Why Doves' Wings and Not Other Birds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אלישע said doves' wings in particular, rather than the wings of another bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about doves' wings from other birds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the dove was chosen. This sets up the final explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע could have named any bird. The גמרא assumes the choice of a dove carries meaning and asks what it is.

phrases.english: And what is different about doves' wings
from other birds?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה מִשְּׁאָר עוֹפוֹת?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail in the story of step 12.

steps.title: ישראל Is Like a Dove: מצוות Protect Them
steps.stepSummary: כנסת ישראל is compared to a dove. Just as a dove's wings protect it, the מצוות protect ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because כנסת ישראל is compared to a dove, as it says: 'The wings of a dove covered with silver.' Just as a dove's wings protect it, so too ישראל, the מצוות protect them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that compares the Jewish people to a dove. A dove is protected by its wings, and the Jewish people are protected by מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle fits the story perfectly. אלישע risked his life for the מצוה of תפילין, and that same מצוה, turned into 'wings,' is what protected him. The dove image shows that מצוות are the Jewish people's shield.
steps.whatToRemember: אלישע בעל כנפים is the model of a clean body for תפילין. His תפילין became doves' wings, because ישראל is like a dove: as its wings protect it, the מצוות protect ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the thread of אגדה with a lasting message: keeping מצוות, even at great risk, is itself the source of protection.

phrases.english: Because there is compared
the congregation of Israel to a dove,
as it is said: 'The wings of a dove covered with silver, etc.'
Just as a dove, its wings protect it,
so too Israel, the מצוות protect them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 using a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישראל is likened to a dove: as its wings protect it, the מצוות protect ישראל.

steps.title: Which material was רבי יהודה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier משנה and asks whether רבי יהודה's ruling refers to the carpenter's wood-shavings or to the flax chaff.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'in a carpenter's wood-shavings, etc.' A question was asked: Is רבי יהודה talking about the carpenter's wood-shavings, or about the flax chaff?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line of the earlier משנה and raises a question about it. רבי יהודה banned the fine kind and allowed the coarse kind, but it is unclear which of the two materials he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed two materials, wood-shavings and fine flax chaff. Then רבי יהודה said he forbids 'fine' and permits 'coarse.' The question is which of the two materials his fine-versus-coarse distinction applies to. The next steps answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised before them (the scholars)
is standing on, i.e., is referring to

phrases.english: 'In a carpenter's wood-shavings, etc.'
A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַנְּסוֹרֶת שֶׁל חָרָשִׁין קָאֵי,
phrases.english: Is Rabbi Yehuda referring to the carpenter's wood-shavings,
or is he referring to the flax chaff?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אלישע story and returns to the wording of the earlier משנה about wrapping food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which material, wood-shavings or flax chaff, רבי יהודה's fine-versus-coarse ruling applies to.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה meant flax
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying that fine flax chaff is like manure, meaning it adds heat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, fine flax chaff is like manure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. In it, רבי יהודה himself names fine flax chaff.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things that add heat on their own, like manure, may not be used for wrapping. רבי יהודה puts fine flax chaff in that group, so fine flax adds heat. That tells us his 'fine' ban was about flax.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Fine flax chaff
is like manure.
phrases.notes: It adds heat, so it may not be used for wrapping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16 by bringing an outside source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's ruling refers to flax chaff.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה compares fine flax chaff to manure.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי יהודה was talking about flax
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה's ruling was about flax chaff, and it confirms this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that he was referring to the flax chaff. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא and confirms it. The question is closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה names fine flax as something that adds heat, his fine-versus-coarse ruling in the משנה is about flax. The wood-shavings are not part of his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it, conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה forbids wrapping food in fine flax chaff, because it adds heat like manure, and permits coarse flax chaff. His ruling is about flax, not about wood-shavings.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַנְּעוֹרֶת שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן קָאֵי.
phrases.english: Conclude from it that he is referring to the flax chaff.
Indeed, conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַנְּעוֹרֶת שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the proof in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה's fine-versus-coarse distinction applies to flax chaff.

steps.title: New משנה: hides may be moved, wool fleece may not
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that food may be wrapped in animal hides or in wool fleece. The hides may be moved on שבת, but the fleece may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may wrap food in animal hides and may move them. One may wrap food in wool fleece but may not move it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists two materials that are allowed for wrapping food and says which of them may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both hides and fleece are fine for wrapping, because neither adds heat. The difference is about moving them on שבת. Hides may be moved, but wool fleece is treated as מוקצה, meaning set aside and not for handling on שבת. This is usually because fleece is kept to be sold or worked, not to be used.

keyTerms.meaning: we wrap or insulate food to keep it hot

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate questions are in play. First, may this material be used for wrapping? Here the answer is yes for both. Second, may it be moved on שבת? Here the answer is yes for hides and no for fleece. Do not mix the two up.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may insulate food in hides, and one may move them;
in wool fleece, but one may not move it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion was closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hides and fleece may both be used for wrapping food. Hides may be moved on שבת, and fleece may not.

steps.title: How to get the pot out of the fleece
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains how to take the pot out of fleece that may not be moved: lift the lid, and the fleece falls off by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it? He takes the lid off, and the fleece falls away.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a practical question and answers it right away. If you cannot touch the fleece, how do you get the pot out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lid may be moved, so he lifts the lid. The fleece lying on it slides off by itself. This way he reaches the pot without directly handling the מוקצה fleece.

phrases.english: How does one act?
He lifts the cover, and the fleece falls off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical method that follows from step 19's ban on moving fleece.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He lifts the lid that may be moved, and the fleece falls off by itself.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: tilt the basket
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says that if the pot is in a basket of fleece, one tilts the basket on its side and takes the pot. Otherwise the fleece might cave in and leave no room to put the pot back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: With a basket, he tilts it on its side and takes the pot. This is out of concern that he will take it out and then be unable to put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is added for a case where the pot sits inside a basket full of fleece. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gives a special method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he lifts the pot straight up, the fleece may collapse into the empty space. He is not allowed to push the fleece aside, because it is מוקצה, so he could not put the pot back. Tilting the basket first lets the fleece fall to the side and keeps the space open.

keyTerms.meaning: he tilts it on its side

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
A basket: he tilts it on its side and takes the pot,
lest he take it out and be unable to put it back.
phrases.notes: The fleece may collapse into the space, and it may not be moved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a special case, a basket of fleece, building on the ban on moving fleece.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a basket of fleece, tilt the basket and then take the pot, so that the space stays open for putting it back.

steps.title: The חכמים: take it out and put it back
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and say one may simply take the pot out and put it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He takes the pot out and puts it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give the opposing view. No special tilting is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not require the tilting step. They allow taking the pot out and putting it back, even if the fleece moves out of place along the way.

keyTerms.meaning: he takes it out and puts it back

steps.whatToRemember: Hides may be moved, and fleece may not. To get a pot out of fleece, lift the lid. For a basket of fleece, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה requires tilting the basket, while the חכמים allow simply taking the pot out and putting it back.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
He may take the pot and put it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may take the pot out of the basket and put it back without tilting the basket.

steps.title: Which hides did the משנה allow moving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with three חכמים sitting together. They ask whether the משנה's permission to move hides covers only a homeowner's hides or even a craftsman's hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יונתן בן עכינאי and רבי יונתן בן אלעזר were sitting, and רבי חנינא בר חמא was sitting with them. They asked: Did the משנה mean only the hides of a regular homeowner? If so, a craftsman's hides may not be moved, because he is careful about them. Or did the משנה mean even a craftsman's hides, and all the more so a homeowner's hides?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a question. Which kind of hides are we allowed to move on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A craftsman (אומן) works with hides for a living, so he does not want them used for anything else, such as wrapping a hot pot. If he is that careful, maybe the hides count as set aside and may not be moved. The other option is that the משנה allows even a craftsman's hides, and then a homeowner's hides are allowed all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular homeowner, not a professional
A craftsman (here, someone who works with hides)
He is careful or particular about it, and does not want it used for other things
We move (carry or handle) an object

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that a homeowner's hides may be moved. The only question is whether the craftsman's hides are also allowed.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhinai was sitting
and Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא גַּבַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chanina bar Chama was sitting with them,
and they asked a question:
Did we learn about the hides of a homeowner,
but those of a craftsman,
since he is careful about them,
we may not move them?
Or perhaps we learned about those of a craftsman,
and all the more so those of a homeowner?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's rule that hides may be moved (Step 19).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's permission to move hides covers a craftsman's hides, or only a homeowner's hides.

steps.title: Logic says only a homeowner's hides
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן אלעזר answers that it makes sense to say the משנה means a homeowner's hides. A craftsman cares about his hides, so they may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן אלעזר said to them: It makes sense that we learned about a homeowner's hides. But a craftsman is careful about his, so they may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: One of the three חכמים answers the question using logic. He says the משנה only allows a homeowner's hides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer is based on reasoning (מסתברא), not on a source he quotes. Because the craftsman is careful about his hides, he has set them aside in his mind, and so they may not be moved on שבת. A homeowner does not care if his hides are used to wrap food.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it is logical

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar said to them:
It makes sense that we learned about those of a homeowner,
but a craftsman is careful about his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 23 using logic.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה means a homeowner's hides. A craftsman's hides may not be moved because he is careful about them.

steps.title: רבי חנינא introduces a quoted tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר חמא starts to give a different kind of answer. Instead of logic, he quotes what רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said. The quote itself comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר חמא said to them: This is what רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבי חנינא בר חמא is about to quote an older authority on this question, and the actual words of the quote continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the answer was based on reasoning alone. Now רבי חנינא brings a received tradition from רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. A quoted tradition carries more weight than logic, so it may confirm or change the answer from Step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said (introduces a quote)
רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוסי, an earlier authority being quoted

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Chama said to them,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said:
phrases.notes: The content of the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical answer in Step 24, this step introduces a received tradition on the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet given. This step only introduces רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's statement, which follows on the next amud.
